sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Simulator 12.6A: Merkle DAG Manifest and Content-Defined Chunking Studio! Adjust the file mutation slider and test Rabin rolling fingerprint boundary re-synchronization versus fixed-size chunking.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, let us explore Simulator 12.6A. Watch how inserting four bytes completely breaks fixed chunking, while Rabin Content-Defined Chunking re-synchronizes boundaries immediately, maintaining over ninety-five percent deduplication!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 12.6.1: Cryptographic Hash Collision Resistance and Rabin Chunk Sizing. Calculate the collision probability bound for one quadrillion dataset blobs, and find the expected chunk size for a sixteen-bit boundary mask.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 12.6.1 time! With one quadrillion artifacts under SHA-256, is the collision risk truly zero in practice? And what chunk size does a sixteen-bit Rabin mask produce?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding! Under SHA-256 with 256 bits, the collision probability is bounded at 4.3 times 10 to the minus 48, which is physically negligible. And a 16-bit boundary mask yields an expected chunk size of 2 to the 16th, exactly 64 kilobytes!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. In the Birthday Paradox bound, M squared over 2 to the power b plus 1 with M equal 10 to the 15th and b equal 256 yields 4.3 times 10 to the minus 48. The expected chunk size is 2 to the 16th bytes, or 64 kilobytes.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Simulator 12.6B: LakeFS Zero-Copy Branching and Deduplication Studio! Create staging branches, apply incremental Parquet partition mutations, and verify physical storage savings against naive copying.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, let us investigate Simulator 12.6B! Notice how branching a 500-terabyte lakehouse repository creates an isolated dev environment instantaneously without duplicating a single byte of underlying S3 object storage.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 12.6.2: Deduplication Ratio and Multi-Version Economics. Compute the total logical storage, physical CAS storage, and deduplication ratio across 10 mutation iterations averaging 3 percent drift on a 100-terabyte base.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 12.6.2! If our base dataset is 100 terabytes and each of 10 subsequent versions adds only 3 terabytes of new data, what is our total deduplication ratio and storage cost reduction?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! The 11 versions represent 1,100 terabytes logically, but only 130 terabytes physically. Dividing 1,100 by 130 gives a deduplication ratio of 8.46 times, saving over 88 percent in physical cloud storage costs!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. 11 versions at 100 terabytes equal 1,100 terabytes logical. Physical storage is 100 plus 10 times 3 equals 130 terabytes. The deduplication ratio is 1,100 divided by 130, which equals 8.46 times.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 12.6.3: Merge Conflict Resolution and ACID Isolation. Determine how Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg serialize parallel ETL jobs mutating disjoint partitions under Optimistic Concurrency Control.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 12.6.3! If Job A updates the March 1st partition and Job B appends to March 2nd simultaneously, why does Optimistic Concurrency Control allow both to succeed without conflict?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Brilliant! Under Optimistic Concurrency Control, commit logs check partition predicate overlap. Because March 1st and March 2nd are completely disjoint file sets, Job B simply fast-forwards its snapshot pointer with zero data loss or blocking!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Modern table formats evaluate partition predicate disjointness during commit validation. Because the file action sets do not intersect, Job B can safely fast-forward its base commit without conflict.
